question: A solid hemisphere is melted and reshaped into a sphere of the same radius. How does the volume change?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Hemisphere volume = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

Sphere volume = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

⇒ Sphere = 2 × Hemisphere

⇒ So volume doubles

**∴ Answer = Volume becomes double**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A solid hemisphere is reshaped into a sphere of same radius

**Formula:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

Volume of sphere = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Hemisphere volume = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

⇒ Sphere volume = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

⇒ Ratio = Sphere : Hemisphere = (4 ÷ 3) : (2 ÷ 3) = 2 : 1

**Conclusion:**

⇒ Volume becomes double

**∴ Volume after reshaping = 2 times original**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Sphere Volume:** V = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

**Hemisphere Volume:** V = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

**Volume Conservation:** On melting, volume remains same unless reshaped differently

**Key Insight:** Two hemispheres make one sphere
